summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontrollers, including a low-level I2C driver and timer-triggered ADC capture, and coordinated FreeRTOS tasks with mutexes on a UART-linked control system. Led a 25-member robotics team and debugged multi-device embedded systems with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Integrated faster-whisper STT (1.0–1.4s), Gemini intent classification (<500ms), TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing, and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction for a 4-wheel holonomic robot on Arduino Due: derived actual heading from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR, 2.9 cm wheels) and fed angular error back into rotation PWM, holding course during translation.

Integrated Xbox 360 control over USB Host Shield with 4x Cytron motor drivers, dual claw subsystems with per-claw IR sensing, and a catapult thrower; added a fail-safe state machine halting all motors on controller disconnect.
